  18. Assumption · funding rounds: round 1 is the ₹40 Cr ask, closed in Q1. Round 2 (₹200 Cr) closes in Q6 and funds organic growth. Round 3 (₹500 Cr, Q10) and round 4 (₹1,750 Cr, Q15) are for organic growth & acquisition; the acquisitions themselves are not modelled, so their cash sits on the balance sheet. All four rounds are counted in cash and in every return shown. Round dates and sizes are placeholders for the founders to set.
  19. Illustrative round pricing: every round is priced at 12× ARR post-money, so the valuation rises in step with ARR. Round 1 uses today’s ARR; later rounds use ARR as 12 × the quarter-end monthly revenue. Returns count each later round at its own price (pre-money ÷ post-money). Scenario inputs, not verified market valuations or term sheets.
  20. Illustrative loan terms. 11% plant interest · 10.5% WC interest. Plant principal: four-quarter grace, then 16 quarterly instalments. Lender terms are unverified.
  21. Working-capital target. Cash tied up in growth increases the funding need. Calculation: ARR × days ÷ 365. Opening WC is assumed funded. This is a planning ratio, not customer credit terms.
  22. Monthly product/channel earnings and operating losses use the same calculation. Funding sums the estimated intervening monthly earnings. Burn is the sum of negative monthly earnings and is not deducted twice.
  23. Exit is at the end of Q16, valued at 12× ARR (the same multiple as the funding rounds) or at 100× annual operating profit (12 × the quarter-end monthly operating profit, before tax, interest and depreciation). Exit equity value adds closing cash, including unspent round 3 and 4 money at face value, and subtracts modelled debt. The lead investor’s cheque is part of round 1 and is valued on the same basis.
  24. Assumption · capex phasing: the spend to Q16 is fixed (₹170 Cr, as the founders set it). Each item is bought in whole phases; a phase adds capacity in proportion to its cost and is paid one quarter before demand would pass the capacity already built. Plan phases: tile adhesive and waterproofing plant 8 × ₹5 Cr (modular dry-mix lines, about ₹1.65 Cr each on the ledger); wood ₹9 Cr before launch then 2 × ₹10.5 Cr; uPVC ₹15 Cr before launch then 2 × ₹17.5 Cr; 20 experience centres at ₹50 L; labs 4 × ₹2.5 Cr, one with each ₹30 Cr of plant; systems 4 × ₹5 Cr and misc 10 × ₹1 Cr on revenue. Phase counts are placeholders until vendor quotes and capacity per phase are in. Dark-store set-up, if any, has to sit inside misc.
  25. User-confirmed model, 28 Oct 2026: RT = city revenue; DD = dealer-zone revenue. Starting and Q16 product cost percentages interpolate evenly across calendar Q1–Q16. Missing channel splits use the available product rates. Waterproofing uses wood’s DD/RT structure as a planning proxy.
  26. Common overhead source: the user’s ₹ lakh/month revenue-anchor table, retaining the ₹128 L column at ₹600 L revenue. Below ₹250 L revenue keep the first ₹61 L budget. Above ₹2,000 L extend each line at its marginal growth from the ₹1,000 L to ₹2,000 L anchors. These extensions are planning assumptions, not validated future budgets.
  27. Cash timing assumption: monthly product/channel revenues are linearly interpolated between quarter-end targets. Quarter-end operating views remain monthly snapshots. Cumulative revenue and operating cash earnings sum the interpolated months. Tax and intra-quarter funding timing are not separately modelled.
  28. Capital cash check: capex, labs/systems and working capital are cumulative closing balances. Cash outflow in a quarter is its closing balance less the previous quarter’s closing balance. Funding deducts those changes and includes operating losses once through the monthly earnings schedule.
  29. Capital return basis: annualised quarter-end monthly operating profit / (cumulative forecast capex + labs/systems + the full working-capital target). Opening working capital is included in this denominator; existing fixed-asset book values are unavailable and excluded. This remains an indicative gross-capital return, not complete company ROCE.
  30. The former 200% represented 60/30 of monthly revenue, not 200% of annual revenue. The revised 365-day annual-sales rule uses 60/365 = 16.4384% of ARR, equivalent to 1.9726 months of the current sales rate. Changing the percentage base alone does not reduce capital twelvefold.
